Subject: VAT on staggered invoices for monthly shipments

Hi Maya,

We run weekly shipments and ShipFlex has asked Redwood to split monthly charges into two staggered invoices (early-month usage, end-of-month adjustments). Our tax team flagged that some legs are intra-EU B2B and others are cross-border to the UK, and they're asking whether Redwood will apply reverse-charge on the EU-to-EU B2B lines and VAT on the UK-bound lines.

Can you confirm:
- How Redwood will allocate VAT per shipment line when we send split invoices
- Whether we need to provide separate VAT IDs per billing entity for the two invoice parts
- Any evidence you need from ShipFlex to trigger reverse-charge on your side

We've attached the draft invoice (invoice_SF-4821-part1.pdf) as an example.

Thanks,
Lydia Park
Finance Operations | ShipFlex Logistics
invoices@shipflex.io

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear summary and the sample invoice. Looping in Ben (billing) and Rishi (tax) so we can confirm treatment and next steps.

High-level: Redwood treats VAT at the line-item level and supports reverse-charge for EU B2B if we have your valid VAT ID and the invoice indicates reverse-charge on those lines. For UK-bound services we will apply UK VAT unless you provide evidence that the supply is zero-rated or subject to different rules.

Ben / Rishi — questions for you:
1) Is a single VAT ID for ShipFlex sufficient to mark the EU B2B lines as reverse-charge if the buyer entity is the same across both invoice parts? Or do we need distinct billing entity IDs per split invoice?
2) What specific customer-supplied documents do we need to store (VAT cert, purchase order, shipping manifests) to satisfy audit trails under the reverse-charge flow?

Lydia — once Ben/Rishi confirm, we can update the invoice template and generate the two-part invoice so the accounting systems reconcile.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, ShipFlex Finance <invoices@shipflex.io>

Date: 2026-08-31T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: VAT on staggered invoices for monthly shipments

Quick reply — summary below and proposed action items.

Summary:
- Reverse-charge can be applied at the invoice-line level if the buyer's EU VAT ID is validated and present on our invoice.
- If the buyer entity on both invoice parts is the same legal entity (same VAT ID and billing entity), a single VAT ID is sufficient. If your flow splits across legal entities (e.g., ShipFlex GmbH vs ShipFlex UK Ltd), we need the matching VAT IDs for each billed entity.
- Evidence: we require the buyer VAT ID, name and address match, and either a signed purchase order or a tax declaration from the buyer. For shipments, having the shipping manifest per line is helpful but not strictly required if the supply is a service (platform access) rather than goods movement.
- For cross-border to the UK: Redwood will apply UK VAT where the supply is taxable there; that requires UK VAT registration on our side (we have that) and we need to see if the customer is registered in the UK for reverse-charge (rare).

Proposed next steps (actionable):
1) ShipFlex: send over a PDF of the buying entity's VAT certificate and confirm the legal billing entity for the first invoice and the second invoice.
2) ShipFlex: indicate for each invoice line the destination country (NL, DE, UK) in the CSV export you send us. We'll map VAT rules by destination.
3) Redwood: we'll produce a two-part invoice template that renders reverse-charge wording on EU B2B lines and standard VAT lines for UK-bound items.

I'm attaching our small checklist for VAT evidence.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Manager, Billing | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Lydia / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the docs. Confirming next steps and timeline: 

1) VAT evidence receipt — confirmed: we received vat_certificate_shipflex_2026.pdf and the mapping CSV. That satisfies our immediate evidence requirement to tag EU B2B lines for reverse-charge.
2) Single VAT ID — because both invoice parts are billed to ShipFlex GmbH (same legal entity and VAT ID), Redwood will apply reverse-charge on EU B2B lines using that VAT ID. No extra VAT IDs required.
3) UK legs — we will render UK VAT on UK_DEST lines in the final invoice; you will see separate VAT line items for those lines.
4) Invoice generation — Redwood will: (a) produce the two-part invoice PDF set, (b) include line-level VAT tagging and reverse-charge wording, and (c) upload both PDFs to your shared Drive link and send to invoices@shipflex.io. Target: 2026-09-03 EOD.

Action items assigned:
- ShipFlex (Lydia): confirm if you want the two PDFs uploaded to your S3 or to our shared Drive link (https://app.redwood.com/drive/sf-4821-invoice). Reply by 2026-09-02 noon.
- Redwood (Ben): produce the two-part invoice template and generate PDF drafts for internal review by 2026-09-02 EOD.
- Redwood (Rishi): archive the VAT cert in our evidence store and flag the account as reverse-charge enabled.

If all good I'll proceed with the generation and we will mark the account accordingly. Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with the invoice links when ready.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
